spark.keyTakeaway: To bound blast radius during partial cluster failures, route each hostname deterministically to one Back Queue with a per-host politeness timer (`10x` last RTT) and cached `robots.txt` rules.
spark.byteSummary:
A naive FIFO queue of discovered URLs fails catastrophically at web scale: links from `wikipedia.org` cluster together and flood one host with thousands of concurrent requests (violating politeness and getting IP-banned), while high-value news pages wait behind millions of low-value forum links.

The **Mercator URL Frontier** splits scheduling into two stages: `K` **Front Queues** ordered by PageRank/freshness priority, and `M` **Back Queues** where a consistent-hash router maps every URL's hostname to exactly one Back Queue.

A min-heap of `(next_allowed_fetch_ts, back_queue_id)` ensures a worker never hits the same host twice within its politeness cooldown, while a distributed Bloom Filter / RocksDB seen-set deduplicates billions of URLs.

decisionFramework.problem: How to implement Distributed Web Crawler & Mercator URL Frontier without hitting unbounded tail latency, state divergence, or operational fragility.
decisionFramework.naiveSolution: Use a single unpartitioned path with unbounded retries and synchronous global coordination.
decisionFramework.whyItFails: Global coordination serializes throughput under load, while unbounded retries amplify transient stalls into full outages.
decisionFramework.alternatives: Compare synchronous strict-consistency paths against bounded asynchronous replication, local caching, or partitioned ownership.
decisionFramework.decision: To bound blast radius during partial cluster failures, route each hostname deterministically to one Back Queue with a per-host politeness timer (`10x` last RTT) and cached `robots.txt` rules.
decisionFramework.tradeOffs: Gains predictable p99 latency and fault isolation in exchange for explicit bounding, observability, and slightly higher implementation complexity.

options.label: Increase retry counts and remove client timeouts so every request eventually succeeds.
options.explanation: Unbounded retries multiply load on an already struggling dependency and exhaust worker pools.

options.label: Enforce strict latency budgets, bounded jittered retries, and graceful fallback or load shedding.
options.explanation: Bounding retries and isolating slow paths preserves healthy capacity and keeps tail latency predictable.

sectionDiagram.title: Blast-Radius & Failure Isolation

cards.label: Crawler Traps
cards.detail: Infinite calendar links (/2026/11/24/...) or session-ID URLs exhaust frontier queues unless depth-capped.

cards.label: Strict Timeouts
cards.detail: Cap TCP connect, TLS handshake, and body size (e.g., 10 MB) so tarpits cannot pin workers.

cards.label: 5xx / 429 Backoff
cards.detail: Exponentially back off hosts returning 429/503 and cap consecutive failures per domain.
